purpose: Use Spinner only for an inline busy mark in a row, log line or custom control that has no loading prop; buttons use their own `loading`, a loading region with a known shape uses Skeleton, and measurable work uses Progress. A small rotating mark that says work is in progress, for a row, a log line or a custom control that has no loading state of its own. It is decorative by default; with an `aria-label` it becomes a `status` region that announces the work, and it stops rotating under reduced motion.
useWhen: An inline busy mark inside a row, log line or custom control that has no loading state of its own.
A small in-progress indicator next to text in a toast or status row.
avoidWhen: A button waiting on its action → set `loading` on `button`, `icon-button` or `highlight-button`.
Content that is still loading → use `skeleton`.
A status with a color and a label → use `status-indicator`.
related: skeleton` — reserves the shape of content while it loads.
button` — renders a Spinner itself when `loading` is set.
bestPractices: Its one prop is `ariaLabel`: size it with a `size-*` class (`size-3`, `size-4`) and color it through the inherited text color (it strokes `currentColor`).

class` on its tag is its sizing API, not a restyle: the spec is a `style_seam`, so `webkit/no-style-override` accepts `<Spinner class="size-4" />`. Keep the class to a `size-*` and, when it must differ from the surrounding text, a text color token.

Without `ariaLabel` it is `aria-hidden`: announce the busy state on the surrounding element (`aria-busy`, a live region or visible text). A standalone Spinner that is the only sign of the wait sets `ariaLabel` (`aria-label="Loading"`); it then renders `role="status"` with that name, so the wait is announced. Do not set it inside a control that already announces its own busy state (a `loading` button).
The spin stops under reduced motion, so pair it with text when the wait matters.
